html:
The world's attention is largely focused on the UN General Assembly, where President Donald Trump's aggressive rhetoric on the ongoing conflict with Iran dominates discussions, even as reports emerge of direct US-Iranian official meetings. The global energy crisis, exacerbated by the war, adds urgency to diplomatic efforts surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

US-Iran Tensions: President Donald Trump delivered an address at the UN General Assembly, threatening to "annihilate" Iran and "drive them into Hell" if a deal is not reached, though he also suggested a deal could come after US midterms. Despite this strong language, US and Iranian officials, including Trump envoy Witkoff and Kushner, reportedly held a "very good" three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation. Amidst these diplomatic efforts, Iran has stated it is prepared to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US eases military pressure and lifts its blockade, following reports of two tankers being hit by projectiles in the strait. However, the US Treasury chief announced that Iran's airlines are to be "shut down" on September 23, with Turkish Airlines suspending all Iran flights until at least March 2027, drawing opposition from China to these "illegal" sanctions. Iran's Armed Forces commanders warned of a decisive response to any new aggression, with the IRGC announcing the destruction of an "Orbiter" reconnaissance drone over Hormuz and a successful test of a weapon to target a US aircraft carrier.

Great Power Politics: US influence and alliances are shifting, with the US signing a defense deal with Denmark at the UN General Assembly to build two military bases in Greenland. President Trump praised UK prime minister Andy Burnham as a "natural businessperson" during their first face-to-face meeting, despite ongoing tensions between the two nations regarding AI regulation, the Chagos islands, and the war in Iran. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres made his final address, pleading for "a world built on interdependence," while French President Emmanuel Macron urged nations to "stand firm" against the "abuse of power by empires." The race for the next UN leader is underway, with Costa Rica's Grynspan narrowly leading an informal poll.

Russia-Ukraine & Europe: Ukraine expressed anger as the EU removed Russian oligarchs Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list, a move Kyiv stated sent Moscow the wrong signals. Russia and Ukraine continue to trade deadly strikes, including a Russian drone attack that killed three children and a woman in the Kyiv region. President Macron called for a moratorium on strikes on civilian and energy infrastructure in the Russia-Ukraine war. Meanwhile, a NATO video from July 2024 celebrating its 75th anniversary is being falsely framed online as "war propaganda" preparing for imminent conflict with Russia.

Global Economy & Technology: The ongoing Iran war is contributing to a global energy crisis, causing "pain at the pump" on five continents. President Trump's financial disclosures revealed over a thousand stock sales and purchases in July, valued between $79m and $270m, including large transactions involving Amazon, Microsoft, and Oracle. In New York, DoorDash agreed to pay $131.5m to settle an investigation into underpaying workers, a settlement Mayor Zohran Mamdani hailed as the city’s largest labor enforcement action. Discussions at the UNGA also touched on digital sovereignty and AI, with Australia's Anthony Albanese advocating for a "digital dimension" to sovereignty, and Macron proposing an "open-source" AI model independent of China and the US, a stance echoed by President Trump's rejection of global AI regulation despite contemplating a US AI task force.

MENA Security & Regional Developments: Beyond the Strait of Hormuz, Iran-backed Houthis are pushing deeper into western Yemen, displacing over 100,000 people and widening attacks on Saudi Arabia, prompting G7 foreign ministers to call on Iran to cease arming the group. Iraq’s Prime Minister Al-Zaidi has vowed to disarm Iran-backed militias, a development Israel is reportedly monitoring. Tensions in the Palestinian territories remain high, with Israeli extremists, including an Israeli minister, storming the Al-Aqsa compound on the eve of Yom Kippur, drawing condemnation from Jordan and the Arab League. Defense Minister Yoav Gallant warned Hamas that if an Israeli is abducted, the entire city of Gaza will be evacuated, following Israeli airstrikes in Gaza that killed Palestinians and a shooting attack in Benjamin that killed Natanel Shkaron. In other regional news, Turkey's Erdogan used his UN address to target ‘gender neutrality’ after recent LGBTQ+ raids, drawing international condemnation.
